role: Sourced library for gates: fail-closed temp file/dir creation and a working-tree mutation lock shared by verify_gates_fail.sh, verify_tests_fail.sh and simulate_ci.sh.
state: env:GATE_TREE_LOCK (default <git-dir>/emuqu-tree-mutation.lock, or $TMPDIR//tmp if not a repo)
toplevel: On source: runs `git rev-parse --git-dir` (errors swallowed) and sets GATE_TREE_LOCK. git-dir is relative ('.git') when run from the repo root, so the lock path is relative to the caller's cwd. No `set` options are changed.

units.does: Creates $TMPDIR(or /tmp)/<label>.XXXXXX via mktemp with an explicit template, verifies it is writable, prints its path; on failure prints FATAL and exits 70 (only the $( ) subshell — callers must `|| exit $?`).
Exits 70 with a FATAL message if the given path is missing or empty.

flags.text: No script calls gate_require_nonempty (repo-wide grep: only its definition and a claim in docs/whitepapers/04-claims-governance.md:289 that it 'exits 70 when an input the gate is about to parse is missing or empty'), so no gate actually guards against parsing an empty log/report with it.

units.does: Creates a temp directory with `mktemp -d -t <label>` and prints it; exits 70 on failure.

branches.cond: mktemp failed or path not a dir

flags.text: Uses `mktemp -d -t "$label"` with no X's — the exact BSD/GNU incompatibility gate_mktemp's own comment warns about. On GNU coreutils it fails ('too few X's in template', reproduced here), so verify_gates_fail.sh and verify_tests_fail.sh abort with exit 70 on any Linux host; they only work on macOS. In verify_gates_fail.sh the lock is already taken before this call and no trap is set yet, leaving a stale lock behind.

units.does: Takes the tree-mutation lock with atomic mkdir; if held by a live PID exits 75; if the holder PID is dead (or pid file missing -> '0') warns, removes and re-creates it (exit 70 if that fails); then writes owner and pid ($$).

branches.effect: FATAL, exit 75; otherwise treat as stale: warn, rm -rf, mkdir (exit 70 on failure)

flags.text: mkdir and the pid write are separate steps; a concurrent acquirer or gate_require_unmutated_tree that reads between them sees no pid ('0'), declares the lock stale and rm -rf's a live lock, after which two mutators can run at once.

units.does: Removes the lock directory if present; always returns 0.
units.entry: EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP trap in verify_gates_fail.sh and verify_tests_fail.sh

units.does: For read-only consumers: returns 0 if no lock; exits 75 if a live PID holds it; otherwise warns that a stale lock exists, deletes it and returns 0.

branches.effect: FATAL, exit 75; else warn, remove lock, return 0 (the leaked mutation is not checked, only a hint printed)

flags.text: The lock contract says it is 'checked by whoever is measuring', but simulate_ci.sh is the only caller; every individual gate run via make ci, gates.yml or ci.yml reads the tree without checking the lock, so a gate run concurrently with verify_gates_fail.sh/verify_tests_fail.sh still measures planted violations.
